destinations.name: Tokyo
destinations.summary: A red-and-white lattice tower inspired by the Eiffel Tower.
destinations.story: Tokyo Tower opened in 1958 as a broadcasting tower and quickly became a symbol of the city's postwar recovery. At 333 metres it is a little taller than the Eiffel Tower, and its main observatory looks out across the Tokyo skyline.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the orange lattice of Tokyo Tower against a violet and peach dusk sky.

destinations.name: Kyoto
destinations.summary: Thousands of vermilion torii gates climbing a wooded mountain.
destinations.story: Fushimi Inari Taisha is the head shrine of Inari, the Shinto deity associated with rice and prosperity. A path of thousands of vermilion torii gates, each donated by an individual or a business, winds up the forested slope of Mount Inari.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of a tunnel of vermilion torii gates leading into a forest.

destinations.name: Mount Fuji
destinations.summary: Japan's highest mountain and a sacred symbol.
destinations.story: At 3,776 metres, Mount Fuji is Japan's tallest peak, an active stratovolcano that last erupted in 1707. Pilgrims and hikers climb it in the short summer season, and it is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage list as a sacred place and a source of artistic inspiration.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of snow-capped Mount Fuji with cherry blossom branches and its reflection in a lake.

destinations.name: Agra
destinations.summary: A white marble mausoleum beside the Yamuna River.
destinations.story: Emperor Shah Jahan commissioned the Taj Mahal in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal. Construction began around 1632, with the main mausoleum finished in the following decade and the wider complex completed later. The marble seems to change colour through the day, from pink at dawn to pale gold at dusk.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the white domed Taj Mahal and its reflecting pool beneath a rose-coloured sky.

destinations.name: Siem Reap
destinations.summary: The largest religious monument in the world, set in a Khmer temple city.
destinations.story: Angkor Wat was built in the early 12th century under King Suryavarman II, first as a Hindu temple and later becoming a Buddhist site. Five lotus-bud towers rise from its central temple, surrounded by a wide moat. It sits within the Angkor Archaeological Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the five lotus-bud towers of Angkor Wat reflected in water between palm trees.

destinations.name: Great Wall
destinations.summary: A fortified ridge-top wall winding across the mountains north of Beijing.
destinations.story: Defensive walls were built across northern China over many centuries, and the best-preserved stretches seen today largely date from the Ming dynasty. The Badaling section, northwest of Beijing, is among the most visited and climbs the ridgeline with watchtowers at intervals.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the Great Wall with watchtowers climbing a ridge above autumn trees.

destinations.name: Singapore
destinations.summary: A waterfront skyline of towers, gardens and a rooftop SkyPark.
destinations.story: Marina Bay was created largely on reclaimed land around a reservoir at the mouth of the Singapore River. Landmarks include the three-tower Marina Bay Sands with its rooftop SkyPark, and the Gardens by the Bay beside it. After dark the waterfront lights up.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of three towers topped by a ship-shaped sky park above a violet harbour at dusk.

destinations.name: Bali
destinations.summary: A Hindu sea temple on an offshore rock, best seen at sunset.
destinations.story: Tanah Lot is one of Bali's most important sea temples, set on a rock formation just off the coast in the Tabanan regency. At high tide the temple is cut off from the shore, and visitors gather on the cliffs at sunset to watch the sky change colour.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of a tiered Balinese temple on a sea rock with a natural arch at sunset.

destinations.name: Dubai
destinations.summary: The world's tallest building, a stepped spire of glass and steel.
destinations.story: The Burj Khalifa opened in 2010 and, at 828 metres, is the tallest building in the world. Its stepped, tapering form draws on desert flowers and Islamic architecture, and observation decks high up the tower look out over the city and the Gulf.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the tall stepped spire of the Burj Khalifa above a hazy desert skyline.

destinations.name: Petra
destinations.summary: A rose-red city carved into the cliffs by the Nabataeans.
destinations.story: Petra was the capital of the Nabataean kingdom, a trading hub that flourished more than two thousand years ago. Visitors enter through the Siq, a narrow canyon, to reach Al-Khazneh, the Treasury, whose carved facade glows rose-pink in the sun. Petra is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the carved columned facade of the Treasury at Petra framed by red canyon walls.

destinations.name: Ha Long Bay
destinations.summary: Thousands of limestone karsts rising from emerald water.
destinations.story: Ha Long Bay in northern Vietnam is dotted with nearly two thousand limestone islands and islets and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Visitors explore it aboard traditional-style junk boats, kayaks and cruises that wind between the towering karsts.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of limestone karst islands and a junk boat with a red sail on calm green water.

destinations.name: Seoul
destinations.summary: The grand main royal palace of the Joseon dynasty.
destinations.story: Gyeongbokgung was built in 1395 as the principal palace of the Joseon dynasty and stands at the foot of Bugaksan mountain in central Seoul. The throne hall, Geunjeongjeong, rises from a two-tiered stone platform. Visitors can watch a changing-of-the-guard ceremony at the main gate.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of a two-tiered palace hall with sweeping tiled roofs before a misty mountain.

destinations.name: Bangkok
destinations.summary: The Temple of Dawn, its central prang rising above the Chao Phraya.
destinations.story: Wat Arun stands on the west bank of the Chao Phraya River in Bangkok. Its tall central prang, a spire in the Khmer style, is decorated with fragments of porcelain and seashells. The temple is especially striking at sunset, lit against the sky.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the tall central spire and smaller prangs of Wat Arun under a violet sunset.

destinations.name: Sigiriya
destinations.summary: A fifth-century rock fortress rising from the Sri Lankan jungle.
destinations.story: Sigiriya, the Lion Rock, is a massive granite column nearly 200 metres high that King Kashyapa chose for his palace in the 5th century CE. The site includes terraced gardens, mirror walls and frescoes, and the summit ruins are reached by a long climb up stairways. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of the flat-topped granite rock of Sigiriya rising above jungle with a zigzag stairway.

destinations.name: Galle
destinations.summary: A Dutch-era fort and lighthouse above the Indian Ocean.
destinations.story: Galle Fort was first built by the Portuguese in the 16th century and extensively fortified by the Dutch in the 17th. Its ramparts, lighthouse, churches and lanes form a UNESCO World Heritage Site that is still lived in today.

stamp.alt: Stamp illustration of a striped lighthouse and fort ramparts with palm trees beside a turquoise sea.
